{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Build

on:
  push:
    branches: [ "master" ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ "master" ]

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

jobs:
  build:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v6
    - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      with:
        toolchain: stable
    - name: Cache cargo dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: |
          ~/.cargo/registry
          ~/.cargo/git
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-cargo-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock') }}
    - name: Build
      run: cargo build --verbose
    - name: Run tests
      run: cargo test --verbose",
  "rationale": "The repository is a Rust project with a Cargo.lock lockfile, so repeated dependency fetching from crates.io is measurable and the lockfile can serve as a cache input key. The measured experiment evidence (batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200, pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE) showed dependency caching reduced elapsed CI time (~20.4%) while preserving all build/test steps. I added a single actions/cache@v4 step for the Cargo registry and git dependency stores, keyed on runner OS plus the Cargo.lock hash, placed after checkout/toolchain setup and before cargo build/test. All original steps (checkout, rust-toolchain, cargo build --verbose, cargo test --verbose) and coverage are preserved unchanged; no permissions, secrets, deployment, or new network access is introduced.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200", "pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
